newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian ex-premier barred from travelling.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian ex-premier barred from travelling.

text.p: Former Bulgarian premier Zhan Videnov has been barred from travelling abroad pending investigation of his role in sanctioning excessive grain exports which led to shortages, state news agency BTA said.

It quoted Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev as saying on Sunday the results of an interior ministry inquiry had shown that Videnov knew the grain balance was threatened but failed to take the necessary steps to correct the situation.

He said new evidence had been sent to the prosecutor general, who last week began investigating former agriculture minister Vassil Chichibaba and three of his deputies on possible criminal negligence charges over grain exports.

Bonev said Chichibaba had introduced a package of measures on grain purchasing and import and export regulations to parliament on June 3, 1995, and had sent Videnov a letter warning of difficulties on July 11.
Chichibaba proposed a ban on grain exports on August 15, but it took until October 20 to come into effect.

"This is a case of criminal inaction on the part of the top echelon of the executive and the necessary investigation will be launched in the presence of evidence of corruption favouring a given circle," Bonev said.

Videnov's Socialist government was toppled last month by mass street protests. The interim cabinet which took office on February 13 vowed to bring to justice anyone found criminally responsible for the disastrous state of the economy.
Bonev said Videnov and Krassimir Raidovski, spokesman for Videnov's cabinet, were temporarily banned from travelling abroad.

In 1995 Bulgaria exported 827,280 tonnes of grain from the 1994-1995 harvest for 7.141 billion levs. A total of 198,933 tonnes of grain were subsequently imported for 6.456 billion levs to compensate for the shortage.
The new government inherited an acute grain crisis dating back to the exports and compounded by a poor harvest last year.
